questions.stem: Which pair of consonants differs only in voicing?
questions.explanation: /f/ and /v/ are both labiodental fricatives; the only difference is that /v/ vibrates the vocal cords and /f/ does not. A voicing pair shares place and manner. /p/ and /s/, /m/ and /k/, /ŋ/ and /θ/ differ in more than voicing.

distractorRationale.a: /p/ is a plosive and /s/ is a fricative; they also differ in place
distractorRationale.c: /m/ is a nasal and /k/ is a plosive; they are not a pair
distractorRationale.d: /ŋ/ is a nasal and /θ/ is a fricative

questions.stem: The sound /ŋ/ in sing is best classified as a
questions.explanation: /ŋ/ is the velar nasal: air passes through the nose, and the vocal cords vibrate. It is the sound at the end of sing, tongue and bank. It is not a plosive, so there is no /g/ at the end of sing in RP.

distractorRationale.a: Plosives stop the air completely; /ŋ/ does not, and it is voiced
distractorRationale.c: Fricatives squeeze the air; /ŋ/ is a nasal, and it is voiced
distractorRationale.d: The voiced affricate is /dʒ/, as in judge

questions.stem: Which word contains the initial consonant cluster /str/?
